Abstract:

Optical burst switching (OBS) is a switching technique formulated for high-speed optical networks. The incorporation of Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) in OBS networks enhances the capacity and efficiency of optical communication systems by facilitating the concurrent transmission of numerous data streams, employing various wavelengths (channels). In traditional OBS-WDM networks before burst transmission, a burst control header is sent to allocate resources, such as wavelengths, along the path. The reservation process occurs separately at each node, lacking an overall comprehension of the network, leading to suboptimal burst scheduling and an increased burst loss probability due to contention this reduces the Quality of Service (QoS). The rigid and hardware-dependent nature of standard control planes in OBS-WDM networks constrains the flexibility of advanced techniques. To handle the challenges of OBS-WDM networks, a software-defined control plane has been developed. The software-defined networking control plane provides logical centralization, programmability, and a comprehensive network perspective, facilitating efficient burst scheduling, dynamic resource allocation, reduced burst loss and delay, improved QoS, swift failure recovery, and overall performance enhancement in OBS-WDM networks.
